rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressed to the Prophet, لو ترى expresses a wish that he see his enemies in their awful humiliation, as consolation for the harm they caused him.
rows.anchor: أن يراد به التمني ، كأنه قال : وليتك ترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, لو is conditional and its apodosis is omitted: he would have seen a dreadful sight or the worst imaginable state.
rows.anchor: أن تكون لو الامتناعية قد حذف جوابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may be generic, as in a saying about someone who repays kindness with harm, rather than directed to a particular listener.
rows.anchor: ويجوز : أن يخاطب به كل أحد ، كما تقول : فلان لئيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لو and إذ use past forms for a future scene because what God guarantees is certain; إذ is the time adverb for seeing.
rows.anchor: ولو وإذ : كلاهما للمضي ، وإنما جاز ذلك ؛ لأن المترقب من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their plea receives no relief: they now see the truth of God's promise and threat and hear Him confirm His messengers; alternatively, they had been blind and deaf and now see and hear.
rows.anchor: فلا يغاثون ، يعني : أبصرنا صدق وعدك ووعيدك وسمعنا منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask to be sent back to worldly life.
rows.anchor: { فارجعنا } هي الرجعة إلى الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A return would bring guidance by compulsion, but God made the matter one of choice; they chose blindness over guidance, so punishment fell on the blind rather than those who saw.
rows.anchor: ولكننا بنينا الأمر على الاختيار دون الاضطرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequel makes tasting punishment the consequence of neglecting the afterlife and failing to prepare for it.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى إلى ما عقبه به من قوله : { فذوقوا بما نسيتم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting means the opposite of remembering: absorption in pleasures distracted them and made them forget the final outcome.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالنسيان : خلاف التذكر ، يعني : أن الانهماك في الشهوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their forgetting is answered in kind: God repays them for forgetting; alternatively, they neglected the outcome and God left them without mercy.
rows.anchor: ثم قال : { إنا نسيناكم } على المقابلة ، أي : جازيناكم جزاء نسيانكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning a fresh clause with إنا نسيناكم and explicitly naming its subject intensifies the threat of retribution.
rows.anchor: وفي استئناف قوله إنا نسيناكم وبناء الفعل على إن واسمها تشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They taste both their present bowed-head shame and grief for forgetting the meeting, and everlasting Hell for their sins and ruinous major offenses.
rows.anchor: وذوقوا العذاب المخلد في جهنم بسبب ما عملتم من المعاصي والكبائر الموبقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the veil verse, fathers, sons, and relatives asked whether they too must speak to the women from behind a veil; this verse was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: روي أنه لما نزلت آية الحجاب قال الآباء والأبناء والأقارب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These listed relatives are not blameworthy if the women do not veil themselves from them.
rows.anchor: أي لا إثم عليهم في أن لا يحتجبن من هؤلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uncles are omitted because they function like fathers; Scripture calls an uncle a father, as Ishmael was Jacob's uncle though called his father.
rows.anchor: لأنهما يجريان مجرى الوالدين ، وقد جاءت تسمية العم أبا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says the uncles were omitted because they might describe the women to their sons, who are not unmarriageable kin.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كره ترك الاحتجاب عنهما لأنهما يصفانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from speaking about the women to addressing them directly signals a heightened warning.
rows.anchor: ثم نقل الكلام من الغيبة إلى الخطاب ، وفي هذا النقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They must observe the commanded concealment, remain within its allowances, guard its limits, and practice piety in keeping them.
rows.anchor: واحفظن حدودهما واسلكن طريق التقوى في حفظهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their conduct while veiled should be better than before, so their inward state exceeds their outward state.
rows.anchor: وليكن عملكن في الحجب أحسن مما كان وأنتن غير محجبات

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God witnesses everything, secret and public, and both the visible and hidden aspects of veiling; no state is outside His knowledge.
rows.anchor: من السر والعلن وظاهر الحجاب وباطنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative reading وَمَلَائِكَتُهُ coordinates with the syntactic position of إن and its subject for the Kufis; Basris explain it by an omitted predicate supplied by يصلون.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( وملائكته ) بالرفع ، عطفا على محل إن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are to invoke God's blessing and peace upon the Messenger, asking God to show him mercy and grant him peace.
rows.anchor: ومعناه : الدعاء بأن يترحم عليه الله ويسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rules that blessing the Prophet is obligatory, then records disagreement over how often the duty applies.
rows.anchor: قلت : بل واجبة ، وقد اختلفوا في حال وجوبها

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some jurists require blessing the Prophet every time he is mentioned.
rows.anchor: فمنهم من أوجبها كلما جرى ذكره

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A prophetic report warns that whoever hears the Prophet mentioned without blessing him enters the Fire and is distanced by God; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: من ذكرت عنده فلم يصل علي فدخل النار فأبعده الله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some require one blessing per gathering even if the Prophet is mentioned repeatedly, by analogy with prostration at a recitation verse and responding to a sneeze.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من قال : تجب في كل مجلس مرة ، وإن تكرر ذكره

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some require blessing the Prophet at the beginning and end of every supplication.
rows.anchor: وكذلك في كل دعاء في أوله وآخره

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some require blessing the Prophet once in a lifetime, analogously to the obligation to profess the two testimonies.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من أوجبها في العمر مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cautious course is to bless the Prophet whenever he is mentioned, in light of the reports.
rows.anchor: والذي يقتضيه الاحتياط . الصلاة عليه عند كل ذكر

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa and his companions do not treat blessing the Prophet in ritual prayer as a condition for its validity.
rows.anchor: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه لا يرونها شرطا

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i reports that the Companions considered the tashahhud, including peace upon the Prophet, sufficient.
rows.anchor: وعن إبراهيم النخعي : كانوا يكتفون عن ذلك يعني الصحابة بالتشهد

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i makes blessing the Prophet in prayer a condition of its validity.
rows.anchor: وأما الشافعي رحمه الله فقد جعلها شرطا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By analogy, blessing any believer is permissible, supported by verses saying God blesses believers and directing the Prophet to pray for them.
rows.anchor: القياس جواز الصلاة على كل مؤمن ، لقوله تعالى : { هو الذى يصلى عليكم }

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The passage begins introducing a further prophetic saying as evidence for blessing believers, but its wording falls beyond this segment.
rows.anchor: وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم :

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A prophetic report says God appointed two angels: when a Muslim blesses the Prophet they ask forgiveness and God and His angels say amen; if the Muslim omits it, they curse him and God and His angels say amen.
rows.anchor: إن الله وكل بي ملكين فلا أذكر عند مسلم فيصلي علي إلا قال ذانك الملكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to ask who provides, then answer for them that God provides; this assumes inward assent they may refuse to voice because stubbornness and love of idolatry silence them.
rows.anchor: أمره بأن يقررهم بقوله : { من يرزقكم } ثم أمره بأن يتولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may withhold an admission that God provides because acknowledging it obliges them to worship the provider instead of powerless idols.
rows.anchor: لأن الذي تمكن في صدورهم من العناد وحب الشرك قد ألجم أفواههم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He compares this argument with Yunus, where the polytheists answer that God provides and are told that anything beyond truth is error.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى إلى قوله : { قل من يرزقكم من السماء والأرض أمن يملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also links it to the question who is Lord of the heavens and earth, followed by the challenge of taking powerless patrons besides God.
rows.anchor: ونحوه قوله عز وجل : { قل من رب السماوات والأرض قل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After compelling their admission, the Prophet frames the dispute fairly: one party among monotheists and idolaters must be guided and the other plainly astray.
rows.anchor: ومعناه : وإن أحد الفريقين من الذين يوحدون الرازق من السموات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This even-handed formulation sounds fair to friend and opponent; the preceding questioning makes clear who is guided, while indirectness advances debate with less quarrel and gradually blunts resistance.
rows.anchor: وهذا من الكلام المنصف الذي كل من سمعه من موال أو مناف

words: لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Indirect phrasing can win an argument more effectively and with less hostility, as in saying God knows which of two disputants is truthful and one must be lying.
rows.anchor: ونحوه قول الرجل لصاحبه : علم الله الصادق مني ومنك

words: لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
rows.speaker: حسان
rows.claim: Hassan's verse illustrates the argument's fair but pointed, indirect form: of two opponents, the worse is sacrificed for the better.
rows.anchor: ومنه بيت حسان : أتهجوه ولست له بكفء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: على suits the guided person, pictured riding a fine horse above the way; في suits the misguided person, submerged and lost in darkness.
rows.anchor: لأن صاحب الحق كأنه مستعل على فرس جواد يركضه حيث شاء

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy reads إما in place of أو, yielding either we or you are on guidance or in clear error.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي : ( وإنا أو أياكم إما على هدى أو في ضلال مبين )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols do not hear their invocation because they are inanimate.
rows.anchor: إن تدعوا الأوثان { لا يسمعوا دعاءكم } لأنهم جماد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even hypothetically hearing the prayer, idols would not answer because they do not claim the divinity people assign them and disavow it.
rows.anchor: لأنهم لا يدعون ما تدعون لهم من الإلاهية ، ويتبرؤون منها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative explanation is that the idols would not benefit their worshippers.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ما نفعوكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No informant equals an expert who knows the matter; only such an expert can tell its truth accurately.
rows.anchor: ولا يخبرك بالأمر مخبر هو مثل خبير عالم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's account of the idols is true because He alone is expert in the matter He reports.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أن هذا الذي أخبرتكم به من حال الأوثان هو الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is read with either yāʾ or tāʾ: يدعون or تدعون.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( يدعون ) ، بالياء والتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite form presents people as the class of the needy because their weakness makes their dependence acute; an indefinite form would mean merely some needy people.
rows.anchor: قصد بذلك أن يريهم أنهم لشدة افتقارهم إليه هم جنس الفقراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human weakness underlies this intensified need, as affirmed by the verses saying humanity was created weak and created from weakness.
rows.anchor: وقد شهد الله سبحانه على الإنسان بالضعف في قوله : { وخلق الإنسان ضعيفا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حميد adds that wealth alone benefits no one unless its possessor is generous and beneficent; recipients then praise their benefactor, who merits praise.
rows.anchor: وليس كل غني نافعا بغناه إلا إذا كان الغني جوادا منعما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the following verse, بعزيز means beyond God's power or impossible for Him.
rows.anchor: بممتنع ، وهذا غضب عليهم لاتخاذهم له أندادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following verse warns in anger against assigning God partners, denying His signs, and disobeying Him; if people turn away, God replaces them with others.
rows.anchor: وهذا غضب عليهم لاتخاذهم له أندادا ، وكفرهم بآياته ومعاصيهم

words: إن يشأ يذهبكم ويأت بخلق جديد
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God will create after them people who worship Him without associating anything with Him.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : يخلق بعدكم من يعبده لا يشرك به شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنا نحن means that God will resurrect people after their death.
rows.anchor: { إنا نحن } نبعثهم بعد مماتهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets bringing them to life as bringing them from idolatry into faith.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : إحياؤهم : أن يخرجهم من الشرك إلى الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God records their prior good and bad deeds and continuing effects, such as useful knowledge, books, endowments, buildings, or harmful taxes, coinage, and practices.
rows.anchor: وما هلكوا عنه من أثر حسن ، كعلم علموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links what people leave behind to the verse saying that a person will be told what he sent ahead and left behind.
rows.anchor: ونحوه قوله تعالى : { ينبأ الإنسان يومئذ بما قدم وأخر }

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes آثارهم as the footsteps of people walking to mosques.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هي آثار المشائين إلى المساجد

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir reports that Banu Salama planned to move nearer the mosque; the Prophet told them to stay, since their footsteps were recorded, and they accepted the distance.
rows.anchor: وعن جابر : أردنا النقلة إلى المسجد والبقاع حوله خالية

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz says that if God overlooked anything, He would overlook footsteps erased by the winds.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر بن عبد العزيز : لو كان الله مغفلا شيئا لأغفل هذه الآثار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الإمام refers to the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: والإمام : اللوح . وقرىء : ( ويكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading has the verb passive, يُكْتَبُ, and reads كل شيء in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( ويكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم ) على البناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مثل derives from usage meaning an example or things of one kind; ضرب لهم مثلا means recount the striking story of the town's people, with the second مثلاً explaining the first.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : واضرب لهم مثلا مثل أصحاب القرية ، أي : اذكر لهم قصة عجيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذ is in apposition to أصحاب القرية.
rows.anchor: وانتصاب إذ بأنه بدل من أصحاب القرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The town is Antioch, and its people worshipped idols.
rows.anchor: والقرية أنطاكية . و { المرسلون } رسل عيسى عليه السلام إلى أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus's emissaries were sent to invite the people to the truth; near the city they met Habib the carpenter tending goats, and told him their mission.
rows.anchor: و { المرسلون } رسل عيسى عليه السلام إلى أهلها ، بعثهم دعاة إلى الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Habib asked for a sign; the messengers healed the sick, blind, and leprous, including his son, ill for two years; Habib believed, news spread, and many were healed.
rows.anchor: وكان له ولد مريض من سنتين فمسحاه ، فقام ، فآمن حبيب وفشا الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king asked whether there was a god besides their idols; they answered that God created him and his idols. He delayed judgment, the people attacked them, or, in another view, imprisoned them.
rows.anchor: وقال لهما : ألنا إلاه سوى آلهتنا ؟ قالا : نعم من أوجدك وآلهتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus then sent Shimon, who entered in disguise, befriended the king's courtiers, and won the king's trust before persuading him to summon the two messengers.
rows.anchor: ثم بعث عيسى عليه السلام شمعون ؛ فدخل متنكرا وعاشر حاشية الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asked who sent them, the two said God, creator of everything without partner; the king asked for a concise description, and they said He does as He wills and rules as He chooses.
rows.anchor: قالا : الله الذي خلق كل شيء وليس له شريك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asked for a sign, they promised whatever the king wished; they prayed for a boy whose eyes were gone, restored his sight, and placed two pellets in the sockets that became seeing eyes.
rows.anchor: فدعا بغلام مطموس العينين ، فدعوا الله حتى انشق له بصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shimon challenged the king to ask his own god for such a wonder; the king admitted it neither sees nor hears nor harms nor benefits, while Shimon secretly worshipped with the messengers at the idol.
rows.anchor: إن إلاهنا لا يبصر ولا يسمع ولا يضر ولا ينفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king said he would believe if their God revived a dead person; a boy dead seven days rose, warned of the seven valleys of Fire, and urged them to believe.
rows.anchor: فدعوا بغلام مات من سبعة أيام فقام وقال : إني أدخلت في سبعة أودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boy said heaven's gates opened and a handsome youth interceded for the three; Shimon identified the two messengers, astonishing the king.
rows.anchor: وقال : فتحت أبواب السماء فرأيت شابا حسن الوجه يشفع لهؤلاء الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing his words move the king, Shimon advised him; he and some people believed, while Gabriel's cry destroyed those who refused.
rows.anchor: فلما رأى شمعون أن قوله قد أثر فيه نصحه فآمن وآمن معه قوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فعززنا means strengthened; usage also applies the root to rain compacting earth and to a camel becoming strong in flesh.
rows.anchor: المطر يعزز الأرض إذا لبدها وشدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A light reading from عَزَّهُ يَعِزُّهُ means that God overcame and defeated the opponents.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : بالتخفيف من عزه يعزه : إذا غلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third messenger is Shimon.
rows.anchor: فغلبنا وقهرنا { بثالث } وهو شمعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct object is omitted to focus on Shimon and the subtle strategy by which truth prevailed and falsehood was humbled.
rows.anchor: لأن الغرض ذكر المعزز به وهو شمعون وما لطف فيه من التدبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As in saying the ruler judged justly, the parties judged can be omitted because the focus is the manner of judgment.
rows.anchor: ونظيره قولك : حكم السلطان اليوم بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بشر is nominative here, unlike بشرا in Yusuf 31, because إلا cancels negation and leaves ما without the شبه-ليس inflectional effect.
rows.anchor: إنما رفع بشر هنا ونصب في قوله : { ما هاذا بشرا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first declaration lacks extra emphasis because it begins the report; after rejection, the second adds لَ to answer their denial.
rows.anchor: لأن الأول ابتداء إخبار ، والثاني جواب عن إنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تطيرنا means that they took the messengers as an ill omen.
rows.anchor: تطيرنا بكم } تشاءمنا بكم ، وذلك أنهم كرهوا دينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ignorant people treat what they desire and accept as auspicious and what they dislike as ominous, attributing either good fortune or misfortune to it.
rows.anchor: وعادة الجهال أن يتيمنوا بكل شيء مالوا إليه واشتهوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares their superstition with the Egyptians blaming Moses and his followers for misfortune.
rows.anchor: كما حكى الله عن القبط : { وإن تصبهم سيئة يطيروا بموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also compares it with Meccan polytheists who blamed the Prophet when misfortune befell them.
rows.anchor: وعن مشركي مكة : { وإن تصبهم سيئة يقولوا هاذه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says drought and withheld rain prompted the people to call the messengers an ill omen.
rows.anchor: وقيل : حبس عنهم القطر فقالوا ذلك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains their reply as: any misfortune that befalls us is because of you.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة : إن أصابنا شيء كان من أجلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant طيركم makes their own disbelief, or their disbelief and sins, the cause of their ill fortune.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( طيركم ) أي سبب شؤمكم معكم وهو كفرهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads أطيركم, meaning your superstition or ominous attribution.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( أطيركم ) أي تطيركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading uses interrogative hamza with a conditional particle, asking whether they take the reminder as an omen; another uses two hamzas with أن and means because they were reminded.
rows.anchor: بمهزة الاستفهام وحرف الشرط . وآثن بألف بينهما ، بمعنى : أتطيرون إن ذكرتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with interrogative hamza and accusative أن asks whether they became superstitious because they were reminded; non-interrogative أن or إن gives a declarative sense.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( أأن ذكرتم ) بهمزة الاستفهام وأن الناصبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light reading أين ذكرتم means their bad omen follows wherever their mention occurs; if mention makes a place ill-starred, their presence makes it worse.
rows.anchor: أي شؤمكم معكم حيث جرى ذكركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are excessive in disobedience, so their misfortune comes from themselves, not God's messengers or their reminders.
rows.anchor: ومن ثم أتاكم الشؤم ، لا من قبل رسل الله وتذكيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they are excessive in error and persist in delusion, treating God's messengers as omens though they deserve blessing.
rows.anchor: بل أنتم قوم مسرفون في ضلالكم متمادون في غيكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage rebukes denial of resurrection with extraordinary force, exposing persistent unbelief, ingratitude, baseness, and insolence.
rows.anchor: قبح الله عز وجل إنكارهم البعث تقبيحا لا ترى أعجب منه وأبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It recalls that the disputant came from semen, the lowliest and filthiest origin, then marvels that he arrogantly disputes with the Almighty.
rows.anchor: عنصره الذي خلقه منه هو أخس شيء وأمهنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man rides falsehood and persists in arguing that no one can revive decayed bones, although he himself arose from lifeless matter; this is brazen contradiction.
rows.anchor: ثم يكون خصامه في ألزم وصف له وألصقه به

rows.speaker: أبي بن خلف
rows.claim: A report says Ubayy ibn Khalaf, with Abu Jahl, al-Asi ibn Wa'il, and al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, challenged Muhammad by crushing a decayed bone; the Prophet answered that God would revive him and cast him into Hell.
rows.anchor: فقال لهم أبي : ألا ترون إلى ما يقول محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After being insignificant fluid, a person becomes distinct, articulate, and capable of argument; مبين means able to express what is within.
rows.anchor: فإذا هو بعد ما كان ماء مهينا رجل مميز منطبق قادر على الخصام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the objection a مثل either marks its strange, striking story of denying resurrection or its implied comparison about what God can do.
rows.anchor: لما دل عليه من قصة عجيبة شبيهة بالمثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denying God's ability to do what His first creation proves He can do amounts to challenging Him and likening Him to creatures unable to revive the dead.
rows.anchor: كان تعجيزا لله وتشبيها له بخلقه في أنهم غير موصوفين بالقدرة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رميم is a noun for crumbled bones, like رمة and رفات, not an adjective; it needs no feminine agreement and is neither an active nor passive participle.
rows.anchor: والرميم : اسم لما بلي من العظام غير صفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who hold that bones contain life cite this verse to argue dead bones are impure because death affects them after life inhabits them.
rows.anchor: ولقد استشهد بهذه الآية من يثبت الحياة في العظام ويقول : إن عظام الميتة نجسة

rows.speaker: أصحاب أبي حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa's school considers bones, sinews, and nerves pure because life does not inhabit them; they take reviving bones to mean restoring them fresh and moist in a living body.
rows.anchor: وأما أصحاب أبي حنيفة فهي عندهم طاهرة ، وكذلك الشعب والعصب

words: قُلْ يُحْيِيهَا ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنشَأَهَآ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows how to create and is not daunted by any created thing, whether its forms are great or minute.
rows.anchor: يعلم كيف يخلق ، لا يتعاظمه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The green tree kindles fire despite fire's opposition to water and its being extinguished by water; the tinder trees are chiefly markh and afar.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر من بدائع خلقه انقداح النار من الشجر الأخضر ، مع مضادة النار الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A man rubs green twigs of markh and afar, male and female respectively, together until fire sparks by God's permission.
rows.anchor: يقطع الرجل منهما غصنين مثل السواكين وهما خضراوان ، يفطر منهما الماء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says every tree contains fire except the lote tree.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : ليس من شجرة إلا وفيها النار إلا العناب . قالوا : ولذلك تتخذ منه كذينقات القصارين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading has masculine الأخضر according to form; another has feminine الخضراء according to meaning.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( الأخضر ) على اللفظ . وقرىء : ( الخضراء ) على المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares this description with the passage about eating from the tree of Zaqqūm and drinking boiling water.
rows.anchor: ونحو قوله تعالى : { من شجر من زقوم * فمالئون منها البطون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever created the immense heavens and earth is more capable of creating human beings.
rows.anchor: من قدر على خلق السماوات والأرض من عظم شأنهما فهو على خلق الأناسي أقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links this proof to the verse stating that creating the heavens and earth is greater than creating people.
rows.anchor: وفي معناه قوله تعالى : { لخلق السماوات والأرض أكبر من خلق الناس }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خلق مثلهم can mean creating people small and insignificant beside the heavens and earth, or restoring them, since resurrection resembles initial creation.
rows.anchor: يحتمل معنيين : أن يخلق مثلهم في الصغر والقماءة بالإضافة إلى السماوات والأرض أو أن يعيدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الخلاق means abundant in creations and العليم abundant in objects of knowledge; one reading has الخالق.
rows.anchor: الكثير المخلوقات { العليم } الكثير المعلومات . وقرىء : ( الخالق )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أمره means His affair; when wisdom calls for an object's creation and nothing obstructs it, He says كن and it comes into existence without delay.
rows.anchor: { إنما أمره } إنما شأنه { إذا أراد شيئا } إذا دعاه داعي حكمة إلى تكوينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command كن فيكون is metaphor and representation: created things cannot resist God's power, like an obedient person responding to a master.
rows.anchor: هو مجاز من الكلام وتمثيل ، لأنه لا يمتنع عليه شيء من المكونات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative reading makes فهو يكون a subject-predicate clause parallel to أن يقول له كن; the accusative coordinates فيكون with يقول.
rows.anchor: أما الرفع فلأنها جملة من مبتدأ وخبر ؛ لأن تقديرها : فهو يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's creation requires no bodily contact, instruments, exertion, fatigue, or labor; His power and knowledge suffice to bring an object into being.
rows.anchor: من المباشرة بمحال القدرة ، واستعمال الآلات ، وما يتبع ذلك من المشقة والتعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فسبحان declares God free of what the polytheists ascribed to Him and expresses amazement at their words.
rows.anchor: تنزيه له مما وصفه به المشركون ، وتعجيب من أن يقولوا فيه ما قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ملكوت means that God owns everything and governs it according to His will and wisdom.
rows.anchor: هو مالك كل شيء والمتصرف فيه بمواجب مشيئته وقضايا حكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The variants ملكة كل شيء and ملك كل شيء have the same meaning as ملكوت كل شيء.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( ملكة كل شيء ) وملك كل شيء . والمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ترجعون is read with either a prefixed damma or fatha.
rows.anchor: واحد { ترجعون } بضم التاء وفتحها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says he did not understand why Yasin's merits and recitation were specially emphasized until he realized it was because of this verse.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : كنت لا أعلم ما روي في فضائل يس
